question: Do I need a permit to replace my bathroom floor tiles?
answer:
Yes, you need a permit to replace your bathroom floor tiles. According to the HDB Renovation Guidelines, replacement of floor finishes such as tiles requires a permit. Additionally, when replacing bathroom floor finishes, you must use pre-packed waterproofing screed and waterproofing membrane with a minimum 150mm upturn against the walls and kerbs to prevent water seepage. Also, UPVC floor trap grating with a long collar must be used at the floor traps, and gas pipes must not be embedded in the floor screed or finishes.

For full details, please refer to the "Floor finishes" section of the HDB Renovation Guidelines:  
[Floor finishes](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/managing-my-home/renovation-and-maintenance/renovation/renovation-guidelines/building-works)

question: I'm planning to hack a wall, replace my windows, and install aircon. What permits do I need?
answer:
Here is what you need to know about permits for your planned renovation:

1. Hacking a wall: The evidence does not specifically mention "hacking" a wall, but it does cover erection of new walls and wall finishes. For replacing windows, it mentions that work within the sold recess area (which includes windows) requires a permit. For hacking or demolition of walls, if it involves non-load bearing walls within the sold recess area, a permit is required. If the wall is structural or load-bearing, you must consult HDB or a professional. So, if your hacking involves non-load bearing walls or work in the sold recess area, you will need a permit. [Sold recess area](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/managing-my-home/renovation-and-maintenance/renovation/renovation-guidelines/building-works)

2. Replacing windows: This is considered work within the sold recess area and requires a permit. [Sold recess area](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/managing-my-home/renovation-and-maintenance/renovation/renovation-guidelines/building-works)

3. Installing air-conditioner: Whether you need a permit depends on your flat’s electrical main switch capacity and the type of electrical work:
- If your flat has a 40 amps main switch or is upgraded under MUP/HIP, installing aircon using existing approved power points or isolators does NOT require a permit. Installing using new power points or isolators also does NOT require a permit. [Flats with 40 amps main switch](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/managing-my-home/renovation-and-maintenance/renovation/renovation-guidelines/air-conditioner-installation-works)
- If your flat has a 30 amps main switch, installing aircon using existing approved power points or isolators does NOT require a permit. But if you need to install new power points or isolators, you DO need to apply for an electrical permit before installation. [Flats with 30 amps main switch](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/managing-my-home/renovation-and-maintenance/renovation/renovation-guidelines/air-conditioner-installation-works)

Summary:
- You need a permit for hacking walls if it involves non-load bearing walls or work in the sold recess area.
- You need a permit to replace windows (sold recess area).
- For aircon installation, permit requirements depend on your flat’s electrical capacity and whether you use existing or new power points/isolators.

Please check your flat’s main switch rating and details of your renovation with HDB or a licensed professional to confirm the exact permits needed.

References:  
- [Sold recess area](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/managing-my-home/renovation-and-maintenance/renovation/renovation-guidelines/building-works)  
- [Air-Conditioner Installation - Flats with 40 amps main switch](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/managing-my-home/renovation-and-maintenance/renovation/renovation-guidelines/air-conditioner-installation-works)  
- [Air-Conditioner Installation - Flats with 30 amps main switch](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/managing-my-home/renovation-and-maintenance/renovation/renovation-guidelines/air-conditioner-installation-works)

question: What electrical works in my HDB flat require a permit from HDB?
answer:
In your HDB flat, you need to obtain a permit from HDB before carrying out certain types of electrical work. Specifically, you must seek HDB’s approval before starting electrical works that involve:

- Electrical items that are not listed in the official guidelines
- Technical details that differ from the guidelines provided by HDB

All electrical works must follow HDB’s guidelines regardless of whether a permit is required. If you do electrical work that requires a permit without getting one, or if you do not follow the guidelines, it will be considered unauthorized work, and you will need to remove or fix it to restore your flat to its original condition.

For example, new 15 amps power points or 20 amps isolators for air-conditioners, additional lighting points, fan points, or rewiring generally do not require a permit if they follow the guidelines (such as no embedding wiring in reinforced concrete slabs or walls). However, if your work involves items or technical details outside these guidelines, a permit is required.

You should always check with HDB if you are unsure whether your planned electrical work needs a permit.

For full details, please refer to the "Terms and conditions" and "Electrical works that do not require a permit" sections in the HDB Renovation Guidelines – Electrical Works:  
[HDB Renovation Guidelines – Electrical Works](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/managing-my-home/renovation-and-maintenance/renovation/renovation-guidelines/electrical-works)

question: Can I renovate the bathroom in my new BTO flat? Are there any restrictions?
answer:
Yes, you can renovate the bathroom in your new BTO flat, but there are some important restrictions and conditions to follow:

1. **Bathroom Enlargement**: You can only enlarge the bathroom or toilet after the first 3 years from the completion of the block. The maximum extension allowed is 600mm in width and 0.6 square meters in area. The extended area can only be used as a dry area (for example, to install a wash basin or shelves). Also, the existing gas riser and its branch pipe must not be enclosed in the extended bathroom/toilet. A permit is required for this work.  
2. **Bathroom Vent Replacement**: If you replace the bathroom or toilet vent, you need a permit. The glass louvers used must be at least 6mm thick, wire-glass type, and have an aluminium U-channel cleat safety device on every glass louvre.  
3. **Installation of Bath and Shower Items**:  
   - Shower screens can be installed but the floor slab must not be tampered with.  
   - Long baths are not allowed if they require extending the toilet. The void beneath the bath must be kept and not filled with cement or other materials. Inspection openings and weep holes must be provided.  
   - Shower trays have similar restrictions: the void beneath must be kept and weep holes provided, with no tampering of the floor slab.  
   - Spa pools must be ready-made, installed only within the original bathroom/toilet area, and must not exceed 400kg total weight. The floor slab must not be tampered with, and proper drainage must be provided.  
4. **General Building Work**: Construction of a cement mortar kerb in the bathroom/toilet up to 100mm height and width does not require a permit.  
5. **Permit Requirements**: Some works require permits, so you should check with HDB before starting renovation.

In summary, you can renovate your bathroom but must follow these restrictions, especially regarding size, structural changes, and materials used. Always check with HDB for permits and detailed approval conditions before starting work.

For full details, see:  
- [Bathroom and toilet](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/managing-my-home/renovation-and-maintenance/renovation/renovation-guidelines/building-works)  
- [Bath and shower](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/managing-my-home/renovation-and-maintenance/renovation/renovation-guidelines/water-and-sanitary-plumbing-works-and-gas-works)

question: Can I hack a load-bearing wall in my HDB flat?
answer:
No, you cannot hack or tamper with load-bearing walls in your HDB flat. According to HDB renovation guidelines, all existing reinforced concrete (RC) structures, which include load-bearing walls, must not be tampered with during renovation works. Any demolition or alteration of walls requires HDB’s approval, and load-bearing walls are considered part of these reinforced concrete structures that must remain intact for safety reasons. If you plan any demolition or alteration, you must obtain approval and ensure that no RC structures are affected. If steel bars are found during demolition, work must stop immediately and HDB must be informed [Walls](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/managing-my-home/renovation-and-maintenance/renovation/renovation-guidelines/building-works) [Walls](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/managing-my-home/renovation-and-maintenance/renovation/renovation-guidelines/building-works).

For your safety and compliance, always consult HDB or a licensed professional before proceeding.

question: Can I change the pipes in my flat?
answer:
Yes, you can change the pipes in your HDB flat, but there are important rules to follow:

- Replacement of existing PVC water pipes with copper or stainless steel pipes is allowed, but the work must comply with PUB (Public Utilities Board) requirements.
- Any work involving installing, fixing, altering, replacing, or removing discharge pipes, ventilating pipes, or water pipes must be done by a PUB Licensed Plumber.
- Concealed waste or water pipes embedded in the floor slab or wall must not have the floor slab or wall tampered with.
- Pipes can be embedded within floor finishes but not inside the floor slab itself.
- If you enclose or encase service ducts or piping (except gas pipes), you must provide a removable access opening of at least 600mm x 600mm for inspection and maintenance.
- For gas pipes, all gas pipe alterations must be done by City Energy Pte Ltd or a Licensed Gas Service Worker, and gas pipes must not be embedded in common partition walls.

In summary, pipe changes are possible but must be done carefully by licensed professionals and follow specific guidelines to avoid damage and ensure safety.

For full details, see [HDB Renovation Guidelines – Water, Sanitary Plumbing and Gas Works](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/managing-my-home/renovation-and-maintenance/renovation/renovation-guidelines/water-and-sanitary-plumbing-works-and-gas-works).
